A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe Invert4TVG and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. v1 ends with references; v2 includes Appendices A-F. The retained material and additions support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding results on three benchmarks, task and reward ablations, and a task-probability sensitivity study.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds pairwise task ablations, initialization results, computational measurements, and qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix D introduces an optional Invert-SFT initialization variant that trains on ground-truth clips and corresponding queries before RL. The main three-task GRPO procedure and 80/20 sampling remain unchanged. Explicit SpaCy normalization clarifies the existing tense-invariant rewards rather than establishing a changed matching procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions report the same Charades-STA, ActivityNet, and QVHighlights coverage and the same grounding and inversion tasks. The added ablations and qualitative cases do not establish a new dataset, evaluation population, or task requirement beyond the retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Only-TVG, identified as Time-R1, to the task-combination comparison alongside three new pairwise task variants. Time-R1 already appears elsewhere in v1. The main comparator sets in Table 1 and Figure 4 remain unchanged; newly cited NumPro is not evaluated.

E3.justification: New experimental controls compare two-task combinations and models with versus without Invert-SFT initialization. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, backbones, and frame sampling remain unchanged. The newly specified two-epoch budget and batch size document settings rather than establish that existing experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's single-task, probability, and reward ablations, v2 adds all three pairwise task combinations, an initialization study, computational-overhead analysis, and seven additional success cases plus a failure case. These substantially expand the investigation of component interactions, efficiency, and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix C's numpy.random disclosure concerns task sampling, not repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores, reward-ablation results, and probability-sweep values are retained. Substantial new results include pairwise R1@0.7 scores of 43.6 for AR+VD, 43.8 for VC+AR, and 42.1 for VC+VD; initialization results of 18.0 versus 17.8 initially and 57.9 for both trained variants; resource measurements; and additional qualitative grounding outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds single-task and joint objectives, a semantic-alignment lemma and proof, a Pareto-superiority theorem and proof, and a generalization-bound corollary. This is a substantial theoretical addition beyond v1's task, reward, and GRPO definitions.

C1.justification: v2's Introduction newly attributes most remaining grounding errors to incorrect action understanding, strengthening v1's more general argument that IoU optimization can impair understanding. The central inversion-task contributions, reuse of existing annotations, and reported 7.1-point Charades-STA gain remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of pairwise complementarity, initialization convergence, dataset complexity, and computational overhead. Appendix E expands mechanism explanations and identifies failure on the qualifier again. The explicit v1 discussion opposing contrastive learning and masked-frame modeling is removed. The new complementarity discussion overstates one result: VC+AR and Only-AR both score 43.8 at R1@0.7.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C add pseudocode, two training epochs, batch size four, eight 40GB A100 GPUs, CUDA 11.8, Python 3.10, offline preprocessing information, and detailed timing and memory measurements. SpaCy root-form matching is also clarified. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wu et al.'s NumPro and describes its frame-numbering approach, modestly expanding the discussion of frame-based grounding. Updated author lists and the changed TimeSuite bibliographic entry refer to already cited works rather than additional research.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the Introduction are rewritten, related work is incorporated into the Introduction, and the standalone alternatives discussion is removed. Numbered sections, organized appendices, affiliations, acknowledgments, and disclosure statements substantially restructure the document.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column to single-column presentation and moves Figure 1 before the abstract. It revises Figure 1 annotations, corrects Figure 2's Video Completion label to Verb Completion, expands Table 2, and adds an algorithm display, three resource tables, and Figures 6-14.

improvement.justification: The added implementation details, pairwise and initialization controls, and explicit failure case improve reproducibility and empirical transparency. However, Appendix B introduces guarantees its arguments do not establish: nonnegative auxiliary rewards do not prove semantic improvement, the asserted KL decrease, or the generalization bound. The new Table 2 discussion also describes a tie as an improvement. These useful additions coexist with substantive new overclaims, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
